report.summary: Reviewed chunk 5 of 5 of canary.py; claims in docstrings mostly kept, one uncheckable, no defects found.

handoff.purpose: History persistence, comparison logic, and table rendering for the canary runner.

symbols.name: load_history
symbols.note: Reads JSONL history, skips unreadable/foreign lines, returns list of dicts.

symbols.name: append_history
symbols.note: Appends one JSON record per probe result; creates parent dirs; returns number of lines written.

symbols.name: compare_to_history
symbols.note: Builds Comparison from a ProbeResult and trailing history entries; computes prior pass rate and regression flags.

symbols.name: _VERDICT
symbols.note: Maps status strings to short display labels.

symbols.name: _delta_cell
symbols.note: Formats delta seconds into a cell string; 'first' for first-ever, '-' for None.

symbols.name: render_table
symbols.note: Renders a compact human-readable table from a CanaryRun; includes summary lines.

claims.text: Read the JSONL history, SKIPPING anything unreadable.
claims.why: The function wraps json.loads in try/except and continues on ValueError/TypeError; also skips non-dict and schema/status mismatches.

claims.text: A half-written last line ... must not take the health check down -- a canary that crashes on its own log is worse than no canary.
claims.why: The try/except around json.loads catches malformed lines (ValueError) and continues, so a bad last line does not raise.

claims.text: Corrupt and foreign-schema lines are dropped silently and the rest of the file is still used.
claims.why: Corrupt lines raise ValueError and are caught; foreign-schema lines are filtered by schema check; the loop continues for all lines.

claims.text: Append one record per probe result. Parents created; never rewritten.
claims.why: The function iterates run.results and writes one JSON line per result; p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) creates parents; the file is opened in append mode, so existing content is not rewritten.

claims.text: previously_passed is "this exact vendor+model+probe has an ok on record".
claims.why: prior filters by vendor/model/probe; oks is the subset with status 'ok'; previously_passed = bool(oks).

claims.text: That is what makes regressed mean "it used to work and now it does not" rather than "it is red", and it is why a lane that has never passed cannot page anyone: there is no evidence it ever could.
claims.why: regressed is computed as previously_passed and result.status in FAILING_STATUSES; if previously_passed is False, regressed is False regardless of current status.

claims.text: An unavailable result is NEVER a regression. We did not ask, so nothing regressed -- the bench being asleep is not the bench being broken.
claims.why: regressed requires result.status in FAILING_STATUSES; 'unavailable' is not in FAILING_STATUSES (it is not in the _VERDICT map as a failure), so an unavailable result cannot set regressed.

claims.text: Latency and pass-rate against the trailing history for this triple.
claims.why: prior is filtered by vendor/model/probe; median latency is computed from oks; prior_pass_rate is oks/asked; the window is applied.

claims.text: Compact human table: vendor, model, probe verdict, latency, vs median.
claims.why: The table header is ('vendor','model','probe','verdict','latency','vs med','note') and rows contain those fields.

observations.what: compare_to_history filters history by vendor/model/probe but does not filter by schema or status before counting 'asked'; however, load_history already validated those fields, so the input is expected to be clean.

render_table uses _VERDICT[r.status] without a default; if a status outside the map appears, it will raise KeyError. The statuses are constrained by CANARY_STATUSES elsewhere, but this chunk does not enforce it.
